title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
statement:
You are given an array prices where prices[i] is the price of a stock on day i.

You may buy one share on one day and sell it on a later day. Return the largest profit you can make from a single buy followed by a single sell. If no profitable trade exists, return 0.

examples.explanation: Buy on day 1 at price 1 and sell on day 4 at price 6, for a profit of 5.
Prices only fall, so no trade makes money.

acceptable_approaches: Single pass tracking the minimum price seen so far and the best profit so far
Kadane-style maximum subarray over day-to-day price differences
Brute force over all buy/sell pairs in O(n^2) is acceptable only as a starting point

tricky_cases.why: prices only fall; must return 0, not a negative number
the global minimum comes after the best sell day; buying at the global min is wrong
smallest profitable case; checks off-by-one in loops

clarifying_questions: Can I make more than one transaction? (No, exactly one buy and one sell at most.)
Must I sell after I buy, not on the same day? (Selling the same day gives 0 profit, which is fine.)
What if no profit is possible? (Return 0.)
Can the array be empty? (No, at least one price.)
hints: Think about what you need to know at each day to decide the best sale ending on that day.
If you sell on day i, the best buy is the lowest price before day i. Can you keep track of that as you go?
Walk through the array once, keeping the minimum price so far and the best profit so far.
follow_ups: What if you could make as many transactions as you like, but hold at most one share at a time?
What if you could make at most two transactions?
What if each sale had a fixed transaction fee?
common_mistakes: Returning max(prices) - min(prices) without checking that the min comes before the max
Returning a negative value when prices only fall
Using O(n^2) nested loops and not improving it
Initialising the minimum to 0 instead of the first price or INT_MAX
